caption:
And the rejection saga continues at yet another famous and overwhelming location in Bondi. We saw atleast 15 groups of people enquire for a table but because this place is so tiny and booked, they had to be sent back. Disappointed faces made us feel bad but excited again as we thankfully had made a reservation. While Anthony Bourdain insisted on no reservations, it does not work that way in Sydney ! 😅

This is ‘The Shop and Wine bar’ in Bondi, a place that has been around for a couple decades and still going very very strong.

You got to wait a little as there are many groups of people who come about “for only 30 mins” to occupy those free tables that are done early. The manager is a very sweet and friendly guy who will make sure you get a good clean table, a blanket if you are cold and great recommendations for food and beverages. He reminded us that they had a happy hour on (on a Saturday 👀) and suggested good options from their happy hour menu which was good for our pockets 💰

The food 🤌

You have to order these 3 things, 
The focaccia, which is around 6 big slices of bread, perfect for soaking up those extra liquids 😅

The meatball with tomato sugo, hazelnuts and parmesan. That tomatoey, nutty texture of this brilliant dish goes very well with the focaccia! Dip it in ! Our favourite was the whipped ricotta. It comes with charred corn, caramelised onions, curry oil, chives and focaccia 😍 The corn and the cream combination is divine 🙌🏻

We were in Bondi, feeling a little healthy so we also ordered the Chipotle Chicken Salad. Its a good fresh salad 🥗 

We could see dish after dish rolled out from the tiny kitchen inside. Wish we get the bar seats next time to see the action. We cannot wait to go back and try the other options on the menu.

caption:
Opened in 1958, 21 Espresso is a Sydney institution located in Double Bay, serving Hungarian and European classics made with utmost care.

It’s around 68 years old now and locals say it’s still serving the same quality of food with huge portions, most dishes churned in house.

You will find the sweetest and warmest people here, welcoming you with a smile. We noticed a lot of families, big and small enjoying their food yet it was not chaotic. No music, just people talking while enjoying their meal !

It shuts at 8.30 pm everyday so bookings are highly recommended especially if you want the main dining seats which have the classic couches and lightings that will automatically take you back to the old days.

The restaurant is known for their warm hearty soups, schnitzels and their crepes so we had to order all of it 😅

We started with their traditional Langos bread which is a fried Hungarian flat bread served with sour cream and a garlic dip.

Hearty chicken soup is what we ordered with the bread which had egg noodles, poached chicken and carrots in a warm chicken broth, perfect start! 

We tried the two piece Gypsy schnitzel which was crispy yet soft with which we ordered the creamed spinach, a must try ! It also comes with a paprika sauce which is thick, creamy and of course delicious ! We also ordered the mashed potatoes on the side, theres too many sides on the menu you can order.

It was our first time so we also wanted to try something more traditional so we ordered the Transylvanian layered cabbage which was a house special. Made of minced pork, sauerkraut, rice and cabbage this was one loaded dish, like a lasagna and equally good.

This was a lot for 2 people but we could not have left without ordering their Palacsintás, Hungarian crepes ! We ordered a single piece of Gundel crepe, made of ground walnut, rum filling and chocolate sauce.

The menu is huge and there are too many other things we want to try, so without a doubt we are going back !

We also tried their mains, Pinsa but fully loaded - The Carnivoro was his favourite (Red base, fresh Mortadella, Italian sausage, pancetta ) and The Potato Patate was hers ( Thinly sliced Dutch cream 🥔, scamorza cheese 🤌🏻🧀)

caption:
Undoubtedly, the best Greek food in Sydney we have had ! This was recommended to us by heaps of people and we finally had the opportunity to try Perama 2.0 !
Elevated decor especially the white walls, vintage wall mirrors and dimmed lights give Perama such a Greek island feel 🏝️🇬🇷 
If you ever walked past this cozy restaurant, we bet you did not know about the massive place they’ve got upstairs (btw this is perfect for large groups as well as date nights ) 

If we were to sum up Perama it would be ‘ Simple and home style authentic greek food ‘ 
Menu is filled with classic Greek family favourites 🫠🙌🏼 We tried: 
🫠Trio House dips including Tarama, Fava and Tzatziki with Pita 🫓 ( you can get one dip or two but the trio is absolutely worth it!)
🫶🏻Mousakka in an iron skillet ( It always amazes us how eggplant steals the show in Mediterranean cuisines and this one was a killer too 💥)
💥Corn ribs (honestly, their calamari is more popular and almost every other table was getting this but we wanted to try their grilled veggies so got the BBQ Corn instead, smoky and spicy 🌶️ with a touch of Mediterranean herbs 🌿)
🎖️DIY Souvlaki (the highlight of the night, an open souvlaki which you assemble. It comes with spit roasted chicken skewers, bread, lettuce, tzatziki and freshly chopped red onions. Charred yet moist and tender chicken skewers were the star of this dish with fresh veggies and zingy tzatziki further elevates the souvlaki) 
🎖️Lamb Skaras (12 hour slow cooked lamb, with meat just falling right off was succulent and the generous sauce was a fab touch ensuring your bite is not dry ♥️💥) Get some potatoes on the side for sure with this dish 🙌🏼

Highly recommend trying this place out if you are looking for something authentic but in an amazing setting 🫶🏻

Also, a huge shoutout to the staff for their exceptional service ! ⭐️⭐️⭐️

caption:
Best castle hotel in Spain?

Spanish castle hotel in a small village called Alarcon near Valencia in Spain!🇪🇸 

This village gave us a glimpse of life in medieval times! Alleys lined with houses leading to the majestic castle 🏰 There were hardly any tourists around and the town was mainly filled with locals. 

Sunset here was magical, the beautiful sun shining on the castle and all its alleyways made it look like a snapshot from another era 🥹 We saw locals gather in the evening, having chats and laugh, the town felt so much at peace ♥️ 

There’s lots of hikes around but we decided to chill and take all the quietness in 😎 

Castles in Spain are called ‘parador’ and we think it’s an absolute must stay when travelling through Spain. We chose this one as it was a perfect pit stop 🚙🗺️between Granada and Valencia 🥰

The Carne Apache (sirloin - salsa macha - taro - jocoque) deserves a special call out! The sirloin and salsa was such an effortless combination, hint of chilli and garlic blended with succulent sirloin. This was ADDICTIVE 🏅The taro chip was a perfect touch ☺️

Large dishes were truly massive, and you are meant to have them with fresh in house tortillas. PS the tortillas are super hot and are served in a cute leather pouch 👝, loveee the attention to detail in terms of presentation! We were looking forward to getting goat but they were sold out so went for beef and chicken instead, both exceeding our expectations 🫠 Beef chop was melt-in-your mouth 👄 succulent and was super addictive. Chicken is hard to nail, risk of it being too dry, BUT the chicken sinoloa style was wayyy too juicy! Hands down the best we’ve tasted recently. 

Service is top notch and the staff is very knowledgeable and helpful so do ask questions! 

Located inside the Eve Hotel, access via elevators 🙌🏻 We would definitely visit again for the vibes, the food and its people 💥✨
